name: Demographic-Targeted Social Bias Detection Benchmark
description: Large-scale web-scraped text corpora used to train general-purpose AI models often contain harmful demographic-targeted social biases, creating a regulatory need for data auditing and developing scalable bias-detection methods. Although prior work has investigated biases in text datasets and related detection methods, these studies remain narrow in scope. They typically focus on a single content type (e.g., hate speech), cover limited demographic axes, overlook biases affecting multiple demographics simultaneously, and analyze limited techniques. Consequently, practitioners lack a holistic understanding of the strengths and limitations of recent large language models (LLMs) for automated bias detection. In this study, we present a comprehensive evaluation framework aimed at English texts to assess the ability of LLMs in detecting demographic-targeted social biases. To align with regulatory requirements, we frame bias detection as a multi-label task using a demographic-focused taxonomy.
reputation: A recent benchmark-style evaluation for demographic bias detection that is relevant to auditing and safety research, but not yet broadly established as a standard benchmark.
notes: Text multi-label bias detection benchmark; likely class imbalance and annotation subjectivity make scores sensitive to label taxonomy and thresholding.
